title: Ummarun Kwabo
content:
Ummarun Kwabo (born 10 March 1954) is a Nigerian businessman, philanthropist, and political figure. He is the chairman of STCC Group of Companies and the founder of UK Jarma Academy, a school in Sokoto established for children orphaned and displaced by the Boko Haram insurgency. He holds the traditional title of Jarman Sokoto in the Sokoto Sultanate and is popularly known as Uban Marayu ("Father of Orphans") for his charitable works.


== Early life and education ==
Kwabo was born on 10 March 1954 in Sokoto State, Nigeria. Details of his formal education have not been widely published.


== Business career ==
Kwabo is the chairman of the STCC Group of Companies, a diversified business enterprise involved in construction, commodities trading, and services.


== Philanthropy ==
In 2018, Kwabo founded the UK Jarma Academy in Sokoto, which provides education for over 176 pupils, most of them children orphaned or displaced by the Boko Haram insurgency. In January 2025, a fire damaged part of the school, and Kwabo pledged to rebuild it with improved facilities.
He has funded food aid and medical supplies in Sokoto, donated property in Abuja for humanitarian programmes, and organized mass weddings for orphans and less privileged families, covering the costs of dowries and ceremonies. His charitable efforts earned him the nickname "Uban Marayu" in northern Nigeria.


== Political activity ==
Kwabo has been active in Sokoto politics for decades. He supported Attahiru Bafarawa and the Democratic People’s Party (DPP) in the 2007 elections, which were widely criticized for irregularities. He later joined the All Progressives Congress (APC), before defecting with his supporters to the People’s Democratic Party (PDP) in 2023, citing dissatisfaction with the APC. His return was welcomed by former Sokoto State governor Aliyu Wamakko. 
Despite political shifts, Kwabo has maintained influence across Sokoto’s political spectrum. He has claimed never to have personally lost an election, highlighting his consistent alignment with winning political coalitions in the state.
In 2025, he was appointed Amirul Hajj (leader of the Hajj delegation) for Sokoto State.


== Awards and recognition ==
Peace Achievers International Award for Humanitarian Service (2020)
Northern Nigeria Philanthropy Award (2021)
Sokoto State Distinguished Service Honour (2023)


== Traditional title ==
Kwabo holds the title of Jarman Sokoto, one of the key traditional chieftaincy titles in the Sokoto Sultanate, which ties him to both traditional and political leadership structures.


== Legacy and impact ==
Kwabo’s initiatives, especially the UK Jarma Academy and his mass wedding sponsorships, have played a role in rebuilding the lives of orphans and vulnerable children in Sokoto State, contributing to social stability after the Boko Haram crisis. His political movements, particularly his party defections and alliances, have influenced Sokoto’s political dynamics. As Jarman Sokoto, his activities bridge traditional authority, politics, and social development.


== Personal life ==
Kwabo is married with children. His philanthropy and political involvement have made him a household name in northwestern Nigeria.
